subject: Post-incident closure: dedicated pool eviction cascade (Orion Financial)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@orionfin.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Incident: warmup/eviction cascade affecting Orion Financial - immediate mitigation and next steps

Hi Daniel —

First, I want to apologize again for the disruption you saw this morning. We detected an elevated eviction rate in your dedicated GPU pool beginning at 08:45 PT and routed a subset of traffic to our warm standby capacity to prevent request failures. That mitigation is still in place while we complete validation.

What we did in the first hour:
- Temporarily routed 25% of Orion qps to warm standby nodes in us-west-2 to reduce tail latency and avoid request timeouts.
- Increased priority for your warmup jobs and disabled an aggressive eviction heuristic for the impacted pool.
- Opened an internal incident channel (INC-20270607-ORN) and pulled in infra, allocator, and autoscale owners.

Immediate impact: higher median latency for long-context requests (~120ms -> 260ms) and a 3% increase in 5xxs during the peak 08:45–09:30 PT window. No data was lost; requests were retried by our platform and most succeeded once routed to warm nodes.

Next steps I own:
1) Share an RCA summary and evidence package by EOD PT (logs, allocator snapshot, latency graphs).
2) Propose a compensation offer for the impacted window.
3) Schedule a short technical review with your ops and our infra owners to walk the evidence and the fix timeline.

Attachments included with this thread: allocator-snapshot-20270607.log, warmup-trace-20270607.txt, latency-graphs-june7.png (see Drive link below).

I will follow up shortly with the interim findings.

Thanks for your patience — we know predictability matters for Orion.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@orionfin.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident: warmup/eviction cascade affecting Orion Financial - immediate mitigation and next steps

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the questions — quick answers plus attached evidence. See the included postmortem-summary-orn.pdf for the short RCA and the Drive folder (https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/orn-incident-20270607) for full artifacts.

Summary (short):
- Root cause: a memory growth regression in the pool allocator that increased allocation latency under a warmup-heavy workload. The allocator-backed queue grew and delayed VM warmups, which triggered our eviction heuristic designed to prevent noisy neighbors. The eviction cascade caused a transient loss of warm capacity that amplified cold-start tail latency.
- Why it happened: a change to the allocator's background compaction code (rolled six weeks ago) introduced an edge-case where certain fragmentation patterns heat up memory accounting; this only reproduces under a high concurrent warmup mix and long contexts (the distribution your workloads exhibit).
- Why the autoscaler didn't fully absorb the spike: the autoscaler observed the increased startup times and entered a cautious scale-up path. Due to the same allocator latency, new nodes took longer to become fully warmed, producing a deadlock-like feedback where the autoscaler limited scale because nodes appeared "slow" to warm.

Actions taken (what we did in the incident):
- Disabled the problematic compaction path for the impacted pool (hotfix deployed at 09:10 PT).
- Explicitly cleared allocator staging caches for nodes in the pool to unblock warmups (09:22 PT).
- Temporarily widened the autoscaler's warmup timeout threshold and added a conservative warmup ramp policy for your pool to avoid aggressive evictions.
- Routed 25% traffic to warm standby while we validated (rolling validations completed by 10:05 PT).

Artifacts attached: allocator-snapshot-20270607.log (contains allocator stack traces and memory accounting), warmup-trace-20270607.txt (node-by-node warmup timings), latency-graphs-june7.png (p50/p95/p99 during the incident), postmortem-summary-orn.pdf (RCA summary and timeline).

Compensation proposal: we propose a service credit equivalent to 5% of Orion's June consumption for the impacted window; we'll open a formal credit request ticket and copy your billing contact. If you'd prefer a larger one-time credit in lieu of on-account credits, Ben can scope options.

Next steps:
- Technical review: Wed Jun 9, 10:00–10:30 PT (aditya@redwood.com, lauren@redwood.com, allocator owner, autoscale owner). Please confirm availability.
- Longer-term fix: We will revert the compaction change and run a canary against a representative warmup-heavy workload; target Q3 rollout.

If you want the raw allocator dump (full stack traces), we can provide it under your NDA; the attached snapshot is redacted to remove internal hostnames.

Apologies again — we take this seriously and will keep you updated.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: allocator-snapshot-20270607.log (log), warmup-trace-20270607.txt (text), latency-graphs-june7.png (image), postmortem-summary-orn.pdf (pdf)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@orionfin.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, ops@orionfin.com
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident: warmup/eviction cascade affecting Orion Financial - incident closure and action items

Daniel —

Thank you again for the patience and the constructive discussion this morning. Quick closure note and concrete action items so we have everything on record.

What we validated in the review:
- Hotfix removed the compaction path, allocator latencies returned to baseline within two warmup cycles, and p99 for long-context requests returned to pre-incident levels when routed back to the primary pool. See latency-graphs-june7.png.
- Autoscaler warmup-timeouts and ramp policy changes prevented the feedback loop in our internal repro environment.

Commitments and timelines:
- Immediate: We will revert the compaction change in the next canary (target: 2027-06-21) and instrument additional allocator metrics to detect the fragmentation pattern ahead of time.
- 30 days: Complete a controlled canary on representative warmup-heavy traffic and publish a short playbook on safe autoscaler thresholds for dedicated pools (target: 2027-07-07).
- Billing: We have opened credit ticket CR-ORN-20270607. Proposed credit: 5% of June usage applied to your account; Ben will follow up on alternate compensation if you prefer.

Requested actions from Orion ops:
- If helpful, please share a short sample job (sanitized) that reproduces your warmup-heavy mix so our canary better mirrors your traffic.

Attachments and links: the full evidence folder (https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/orn-incident-20270607) contains the artifacts we discussed; postmortem-summary-orn.pdf is attached to this thread.

Closing note: We are labeling this incident "Resolved" in our internal tracker after the rolling validations completed and will keep a monitoring watch for 72 hours. If you see any residual anomalies, ping me directly (aditya@redwood.com).

Thanks — we value Orion's partnership and will take these learnings to make the platform more resilient for long-context, warmup-heavy workloads.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
